body: In my opinion, it makes sense to introduce a new AST node, like `FormattedStringNode` (string template and substitution expressions). This would simplify the formatter support in the future, as it allows to distinguish a formatted string from a similar subexpression, and also some optimizations are possible when the substitution values ​​are known at compile time. I have not reviewed the code in detail, but at a quick glance it seems to me that the tokenizer changes are a bit overcomplicated.

> In my opinion, it makes sense to introduce a new AST node, like `FormattedStringNode` (string template and substitution expressions). This would simplify the formatter support in the future, as it allows to distinguish a formatted string from a similar subexpression, and also some optimizations are possible when the substitution values ​​are known at compile time.

This sounds reasonable. I'll take a crack at it. Early work has me running into issues understanding how to update GDScriptCompiler to handle the new AST node. Is there any documentation that explains the various codegen types and patterns used there (address, add/write/clear, stack, parameter/local/constant/name/temporary, etc.)?

Okay, I added FormattedStringNode which consists of a list of TemplatePieces (string literal or expression node). The parser turns tokens into a FormattedStringNode, and the compiler turns a FormattedStringNode into a String::format call. This indeed should make it easier to plumb per-slot formatting through.

We don't use the feature branch workflow on `godotengine/godot`. The pull request needs to be in a workable state and approved before it can be merged.

Having `{}` syntax highlighting is not critical for getting this merged, but the inconsistency between raw literals and f-string highlighting (where the prefix isn't highlighted correctly) should be fixed.

This is the relevant code for raw literal highlighting:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/134da374975114ef8e05cf81d1d30eff645e310e/modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_highlighter.cpp#L600-L603

I tried to update the syntax highlighting, but it looks like my push went sideways. I can't understand the 'Compare' results of the push, although the files look okay. Help would be appreciated. In the meanwhile, here's what I'm seeing on my screen with the highlighting change:

> Not sure about the difference between format_indexed and fstring, but compiling fstrings to something like the non-indexed case might be worth it if it's not too big a change. If we do go with that, it might be safer to use something besides {} for the placeholder argument - I think it's ok currently, but would depend on the current Dictionary -> String behavior of using {  } for empty dictionaries instead of {}

Thinking about this some more, trying to come up with a placeholder argument that we hope users won't return in one of the values doesn't feel right.  Technically there's the same issue with the default placeholder, as values could include something like "{1}", and be replaced again by a later value.  For example, the code below prints "test, test":

```gdscript
var s1 := "{1}"
var s2 := "test"
print(f"{s1}, {s2}")
```

With `String::format`, this behavior is documented, and can be worked around by users providing their own custom placeholder, but I think it'd be nice to avoid this with f-strings if we can.  I'm wondering if we could compile the `FormattedStringNode` to something like `"".join(array of TemplatePiece results)` in `GDScriptCompiler::_parse_expression` instead of using `String::format`
@aaronp64 Good thought. I updated the compiler to join the separately-formatted parts rather than using .format() which can have the unintended consequence you point out.

@aaronp64 Also for your performance evaluation, please also evaluate f-strings with only constant slots (e.g. f"foo {5+2} bar {'xxx'.to_upper()} baz") to see if we're appropriately avoiding the evals and join (it should be as fast as a constant string).

Thanks for the updated benchmarks. Can you check that compile time constant expression evaluation works as well? The expression I noted earlier (f"foo {5+2} bar {'xxx'.to_upper()} baz") should have its slots evaluated at compile time and turn into a constant string.

`f"foo {5+2} bar {'xxx'.to_upper()} baz"` doesn't seem to be fully evaluated at compile time due to `to_upper()` - I tried `String.num(...)` as well, same for that.  They don't seem to be evaluated at compile time outside of f-strings either though, so I think that's ok.  Some methods do get evaluated at compile time, like `max(...)` - I'm not sure what cases are expected to be handled at compile time, and which are expected to be done at run time.

The f-string `f"foo {5+2} bar {max(1, 2, 3)} {f'{1 + 3}'} {Vector2(1, 2)} baz"` is fully evaluated at compile time with the latest code - I think it's doing what's possible at compile time based on what already gets reduced to constant values.

But given that this PR has sat for over a year with no action taken to merge it, it seems clear that the Godot leads don't agree. So I think we have three options here. 1. I revert the rebase changes to put this back where it was yesterday. 2. I close this PR.  or 3. I leave it as it is now. Or maybe there's another path you prefer. Let me know.

I'd say that if it is such an arduous or complex task to do manually it doesn't seem appropriate to automate it in this way, and if you find you are not able to dedicate the time to work on this PR it would be best to close it I would say, as we would require you to follow up any feedback on it

But as this has not been given a decision by the team on if the feature and approach are desired it can wait, but do note that we would require you to participate in responding to feedback and review for this to be merged down the line, so if you feel that you are not going to be able or are interested in spending more time on this that would be an issue

Rebasing this right now is not necessarily critical before a decision on the appropriate approach to the feature is made, but it would aid testing and evaluating of your solution

The complexity of the task was that in addition to rebasing the PR I factored the commits into separately reviewable components in the way that I'd want them factored if I were to review this PR. I did review the changes myself. I've left them here in a single PR until it gets serious interest. 

Regarding my time, I had plenty of free time to help address issues and get this merged in when I wrote it a year ago, but I have different priorities now. I've kept this open because I wanted this capability for myself back when I was using Godot regularly and I've heard other Godot users want this as well. But indeed I won't be able to spend significant time ushering this through the review process now. So if this would require that kind of time and nobody else is interested in adopting this, we may need to drop it.
